q: An 82-year-old man presents with dyspnea and acute confusion but no chest pain. His ECG shows ST changes suspicious for ischemia. How should the absence of chest pain be interpreted?
o: It supports attributing the symptoms to aging and deferring cardiac evaluation.
It remains compatible with anginal equivalents and warrants cardiac evaluation.
It supports attributing the ECG changes to anxiety and deferring cardiac evaluation.
It supports attributing the confusion to dementia and deferring cardiac evaluation.
explanation:
**Anginal equivalents** in older adults include dyspnea and confusion, which may be mistaken for aging or comorbid illness (p. 1136). Ischemic ECG changes are evidence of myocardial ischemia; diagnosing myocardial infarction also requires evidence of acute myocardial injury from cardiac biomarkers (p. 1136).
"older individuals often have anginal equivalent symptoms such as dyspnea, epigastric pain, fatigue, confusion, or malaise that may be misinterpreted as consequences of aging or comorbid illness." (p. 1136).

**A. It supports attributing the symptoms to aging and deferring cardiac evaluation.** Wrong, dyspnea and confusion are recognized anginal equivalents; attributing them to aging can miss the ischemic presentation described in the source (p. 1136).
**B. It remains compatible with anginal equivalents and warrants cardiac evaluation.** Correct, dyspnea and confusion fit the listed anginal equivalents. Applying that description together with the suspicious ECG supports cardiac evaluation; this is a clinical inference, not a confirmed infarction diagnosis (p. 1136).
**C. It supports attributing the ECG changes to anxiety and deferring cardiac evaluation.** Wrong, the source includes ischemic ECG changes among signs of myocardial ischemia. Absence of chest pain does not justify dismissing those changes as anxiety in this presentation (inference, p. 1136).
**D. It supports attributing the confusion to dementia and deferring cardiac evaluation.** Wrong, the source specifically includes confusion as an anginal equivalent and cautions against interpreting such symptoms as comorbid illness; that makes deferral on this basis inappropriate (inference, p. 1136).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1136.
ref: Hazzard Ch 74 — CORONARY HEART DISEASE AND DYSLIPIDEMIA

q: מטופל מתנגד למסירת מידע רפואי עליו, והצוות שוקל מסירה לשם הגנה על בריאות הזולת. אין במקרה הסכמה, חובת דיווח מכוח דין אחר או עילת מסירה נוספת. איזו קביעה נדרשת לחריג זה לפי סעיף 20(א)(5) לחוק זכויות החולה?
o: קביעת ועדת אתיקה לאחר שניתנה למטופל הזדמנות להשמיע את דבריו
קביעת הרופא המטפל לאחר שניתנה למטופל הזדמנות להשמיע את דבריו
קביעת מנהל המחלקה לאחר שניתנה למטופל הזדמנות להשמיע את דבריו
קביעת נציג המשפחה לאחר שניתנה למטופל הזדמנות להשמיע את דבריו
explanation:
**סודיות רפואית** היא הכלל, והחריג להגנה על בריאות הזולת או הציבור דורש **קביעת ועדת אתיקה** לאחר מתן הזדמנות למטופל להשמיע את דבריו. הוועדה צריכה לקבוע שהמסירה חיונית ושצורכה גובר על העניין באי־מסירה; גם אז היקפה מוגבל לנדרש לצורך העניין (סעיפים 19, 20, עמ׳ 18, 19).
"ועדת האתיקה קבעה, לאחר מתן הזדמנות למטופל להשמיע את דבריו, כי מסירת המידע הרפואי על אודותיו חיונית להגנה על בריאות הזולת או הציבור" (עמ׳ 19).

**א. קביעת ועדת אתיקה לאחר שניתנה למטופל הזדמנות להשמיע את דבריו.** נכונה, החריג המסוים שבשאלה דורש את קביעת ועדת האתיקה לאחר שמיעת המטופל, בדבר חיוניות המסירה והעדפתה על אי־מסירה (עמ׳ 19).
**ב. קביעת הרופא המטפל לאחר שניתנה למטופל הזדמנות להשמיע את דבריו.** שגויה, שיחה של הרופא עם המטופל אינה מחליפה את קביעת ועדת האתיקה הנדרשת לחריג. כשאין עילה אחרת למסירה, החלטת הרופא אינה מספקת (עמ׳ 19).
**ג. קביעת מנהל המחלקה לאחר שניתנה למטופל הזדמנות להשמיע את דבריו.** שגויה, למנהל המחלקה אין בסעיף זה סמכות להחליף את קביעת ועדת האתיקה. מתן אפשרות למטופל לדבר הוא תנאי בהליך הוועדה, ולא הסמכה לכל מנהל (עמ׳ 19).
**ד. קביעת נציג המשפחה לאחר שניתנה למטופל הזדמנות להשמיע את דבריו.** שגויה, קרבה משפחתית ושמיעת המטופל אינן מקנות לנציג המשפחה את הסמכות שהחוק נתן לוועדת האתיקה בחריג זה (עמ׳ 19).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו־1996, סעיפים 19, 20(א)(5), 20(ב), עמ׳ PDF 18, 19.
label: Source: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו-1996 · §§19–20, PDF pp18–19

q: A 76-year-old retired biologist visits your clinic and asks about the fundamental difference between aging and development, noting that both involve changes in the body over time. He's curious about why development proceeds so precisely while aging seems more variable. What is the key biological distinction?
o: Development and aging are both directed by equally strong natural selection, with aging following the same precise genetic program
Development is directly shaped by natural selection while aging occurs beyond the reach of strong selective pressure
Development is less strongly shaped by natural selection than aging, because selective pressure rises steadily after reproduction
Development proceeds without natural selection, while aging is tightly programmed to improve survival after the reproductive years
explanation:
**Natural selection shapes development more strongly than late-life aging.** Mutations that impair development are rapidly removed because they compromise animals at ages commonly reached in nature. Selection becomes much weaker against problems that emerge at ages few animals survive to reach, explaining why late-life deterioration is less tightly constrained (p. 4). The source states: "Development creates a healthy young adult from a fertilized egg and is strongly molded by natural selection" (p. 4).

**A. Development and aging are both directed by equally strong natural selection, with aging following the same precise genetic program.** Wrong, equal selective pressure is the wrong premise: defects arising during development face strong selection, whereas effects delayed beyond usual survival ages encounter much weaker selection (p. 4).
**B. Development is directly shaped by natural selection while aging occurs beyond the reach of strong selective pressure.** Correct, this captures the age-dependent strength of selection. A mutation that harms development is more readily eliminated than one whose harmful effect appears only at rarely reached ages (p. 4).
**C. Development is less strongly shaped by natural selection than aging, because selective pressure rises steadily after reproduction.** Wrong, the source describes diminishing selective force at late ages, so stronger late-life pressure cannot explain why development is more precise (p. 4).
**D. Development proceeds without natural selection, while aging is tightly programmed to improve survival after the reproductive years.** Wrong, development is directly shaped by selection. The source explains aging through weaker late-life selection, rather than a precise program selected to improve late-life survival (p. 4).

Source: Hazzard, 8th ed., pp. 4.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p.4

q: A 70-year-old woman receives a result showing peripheral white-cell telomere length below the average for her age. Which limitation is important when interpreting this result in an individual?
o: The telomere measurement is calibrated primarily from DNA methylation patterns
Substantial variability limits the clinical applications of the telomere measurement
Telomeres lengthen with age and provide a measure of reversed aging
Uniformity between individuals permits precise estimation of biological age from telomeres
explanation:
**Telomere length** has associations with aging but limited individual clinical application. Hazzard describes "substantial variability that has limited clinical applications so far" (p. 602). DNA-methylation clocks are a separate epigenetic approach, while aging itself is associated with telomere loss (p. 602).

**A. The telomere measurement is calibrated primarily from DNA methylation patterns.** Wrong, calibration from DNA methylation describes epigenetic clocks, not the telomere-length measurement (p. 602).
**B. Substantial variability limits the clinical applications of the telomere measurement.** Correct, this is the limitation explicitly identified for peripheral white-cell telomere length (p. 602).
**C. Telomeres lengthen with age and provide a measure of reversed aging.** Wrong, the source describes telomere loss with aging rather than progressive lengthening (p. 602).
**D. Uniformity between individuals permits precise estimation of biological age from telomeres.** Wrong, the substantial variability reported in the source contradicts the proposed uniformity and precision (p. 602).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 602.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 602

q: A 69-year-old woman at high cardiovascular risk wants to improve a diet rich in processed foods. Which change fits the Mediterranean-style pattern described in Hazzard?
o: Favor processed meats and hydrogenated fats over fish and nuts
Favor olive oil, nuts, and fish while reducing processed meat
Favor animal fats while reducing oils derived from plant sources
Favor foods containing trans fats while reducing olive oil and fish
explanation:
**Mediterranean-style eating** emphasizes plant-derived oils, nuts, and fish rather than red and processed meats (p. 416). Hazzard describes a pattern that "promotes the use of olive oil, tree nuts, peanuts, fatty fish and other seafood, and white meat" and discourages red and processed meats (p. 416).

**A. Favor processed meats and hydrogenated fats over fish and nuts.** Wrong, this substitutes foods the source discourages for foods it promotes (p. 416).
**B. Favor olive oil, nuts, and fish while reducing processed meat.** Correct, this follows the named food pattern and reduction in processed meat (p. 416).
**C. Favor animal fats while reducing oils derived from plant sources.** Wrong, the source emphasizes natural fats from vegetable oils, nuts, and fish while reducing animal-product fats (p. 416).
**D. Favor foods containing trans fats while reducing olive oil and fish.** Wrong, the source advises avoiding foods containing trans fatty acids, not preferring them (p. 416).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 416.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A 79-year-old woman with diabetes takes metformin. Her eGFR has fallen to 28 mL/min/1.73 m². Considering the renal appropriateness of metformin separately from treatment of congestion, which action follows Hazzard?
o: Stop metformin because the renal contraindication is present
Continue metformin because its hypoglycemia risk is low
Increase metformin because appetite and weight have declined
Switch to extended-release metformin and continue treatment
explanation:
**Metformin is contraindicated** when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m². Its low hypoglycemia risk does not remove this renal restriction; Hazzard also discusses lactic acidosis risk and the need to account for renal clearance (p. 1576).
"Metformin is contraindicated in patients with eGFR below 30 mL/min/ 1.73 m2." (p. 1576).

**A. Stop metformin because the renal contraindication is present.** Correct, the stated eGFR is below the contraindication threshold (p. 1576).
**B. Continue metformin because its hypoglycemia risk is low.** Wrong, low hypoglycemia risk does not override the separate contraindication in reduced renal function (p. 1576).
**C. Increase metformin because appetite and weight have declined.** Wrong, dose escalation does not address the renal contraindication; the source also treats appetite and weight loss as potential adverse effects (p. 1576).
**D. Switch to extended-release metformin and continue treatment.** Wrong, the contraindication applies to metformin; changing its release formulation does not meet the renal requirement (inference, p. 1576).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1576.

q: An older woman takes lithium, and addition of an ACE inhibitor is being considered. Which interaction and recommendation are described in the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Increased lithium toxicity risk; avoid and monitor lithium concentrations
Reduced lithium toxicity risk; expand use of the combination
Reduced lithium toxicity risk; increase the lithium dose
Increased lithium toxicity risk; omit lithium concentration monitoring
explanation:
**ACE inhibitors with lithium** are listed as a potentially important drug interaction. Beers identifies increased lithium toxicity risk and recommends avoidance with monitoring of lithium concentrations. (p. 2070)
"Increased risk of lithium toxicity." (p. 2070)
"Avoid; monitor lithium concentrations." (p. 2070)

**A. Increased lithium toxicity risk; avoid and monitor lithium concentrations.** Correct, both the direction of risk and the recommendation match the table. (p. 2070)
**B. Reduced lithium toxicity risk; expand use of the combination.** Wrong, the table identifies an increase in toxicity risk, so the claimed protection does not support wider use. (p. 2070)
**C. Reduced lithium toxicity risk; increase the lithium dose.** Wrong, the table identifies increased toxicity risk and recommends avoidance and monitoring rather than dose escalation. (p. 2070)
**D. Increased lithium toxicity risk; omit lithium concentration monitoring.** Wrong, the risk is correctly identified, but omitting monitoring conflicts with the explicit recommendation to monitor lithium concentrations. (p. 2070)

Source: 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, Table 5, p. 2070.

q: A 76-year-old man who has received immunosuppressive treatment presents with pneumonia. When choosing empirical therapy, why is it important to determine the type, intensity, and duration of immunosuppression?
o: To narrow the expected pathogens to those found in an immunocompetent patient
To select treatment by age in place of assessing the acute episode’s severity
To tailor the assessment of likely pathogens and treatment to immune status
To defer the choice of initial treatment until the pathogen has been identified
explanation:
**Immune status** influences the possible etiologic spectrum of pneumonia. Hazzard states that the type, intensity, and duration of immunosuppression affect etiology, management, and prognosis. Initial therapy is empirical because the causative pathogen is generally unknown at diagnosis, and selection also considers acquisition setting, resistance risk, and illness severity. (p. 1681)
"The type of immunosuppression, intensity, and duration influence the etiology, management, and prognosis." (p. 1681)
"Differentiation depending on the immunocompetence of the host is essential, as this frequently points to a totally different etiologic spectrum." (p. 1681)

**A. To narrow the expected pathogens to those found in an immunocompetent patient.** Wrong, the source says immunocompetence can point to a different etiologic spectrum, so the purpose is not to narrow the assessment to the usual immunocompetent spectrum. (p. 1681)
**B. To select treatment by age in place of assessing the acute episode’s severity.** Wrong, the source includes the severity of the acute episode among the factors guiding initial treatment; age does not replace that assessment. (p. 1681)
**C. To tailor the assessment of likely pathogens and treatment to immune status.** Correct, these details affect the etiologic assessment and management described in the source, making them relevant to empirical selection. (p. 1681)
**D. To defer the choice of initial treatment until the pathogen has been identified.** Wrong, the source says initial treatment must be established empirically because the pathogen is generally unknown at diagnosis; these details help choose that treatment. (p. 1681)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 1681.
ref: Hazzard Ch 105 — BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA AND TUBERCULOSIS

q: A 78-year-old woman is hospitalized after a fall. Medication review reveals regular oral diphenhydramine use for sleep. Which approach follows the AGS Beers Criteria 2023?
o: Stop diphenhydramine and reassess treatment of the sleep complaint
Continue diphenhydramine and reassess symptoms at monthly visits
Halve the diphenhydramine dose and retain it as the sleep treatment
Replace diphenhydramine with a short-acting benzodiazepine for sleep
explanation:
**Anticholinergic burden** is the reason oral diphenhydramine appears in the avoid category (p. 2057). Beers states: "Cumulative exposure to anticholinergic drugs is associated with an increased risk of falls, delirium, and dementia, even in younger adults" (p. 2057). Benzodiazepines also increase fall and cognitive risks in older adults (p. 2060).

**A. Stop diphenhydramine and reassess treatment of the sleep complaint.** Correct, this removes the medication that Beers advises avoiding for this use; a replacement should be assessed on its own merits (p. 2057).
**B. Continue diphenhydramine and reassess symptoms at monthly visits.** Wrong, monitoring while continuing it does not follow the avoid recommendation for this exposure (p. 2057).
**C. Halve the diphenhydramine dose and retain it as the sleep treatment.** Wrong, the recommendation is avoidance, not retention at a reduced dose for chronic sleep treatment (p. 2057).
**D. Replace diphenhydramine with a short-acting benzodiazepine for sleep.** Wrong, benzodiazepines are also in the avoid category and increase cognitive impairment and fall risks (p. 2060).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2057, 2060.

q:
בת 90, מגיעה להערכה גריאטרית במרפאה. ברשימת התרופות הקבועות:  
 Venlafaxine 37.5 mg X1/d  
 Mirtazapine 30 mg x 1/d  
 Quetiapine 50 mg x 1/d  
 Clonazepam 0.5 mg x 3/d  
 המטופלת ערנית, מתמצאת, ללא ירידה קוגניטיבית משמעותית. על פי ה- Beers Criteria איזו מהתרופות הבאות יש להוריד מינון או להפסיק בעדיפות ראשונה במטופלת הזו?
o: Venlafaxine
Mirtazapine
Quetiapine
Clonazepam
explanation:
Official answer: ד

**Clonazepam and other benzodiazepines** are generally to be avoided in older adults because of increased sensitivity and cognitive and functional risks. Beers also lists appropriate indications; it does not rank these four drugs for a patient whose treatment indications are not supplied (Beers 2023, p. 2060).
"Older adults have increased sensitivity to benzodiazepines and decreased metabolism of long-acting agents" (p. 2060).

**A. Venlafaxine.** Wrong, not the official first deprescribing choice. SNRIs carry a use-with-caution warning for SIADH or hyponatremia, which does not establish the sequence for this patient (p. 2068).
**B. Mirtazapine.** Wrong, not the official first choice. Its SIADH/hyponatremia warning calls for sodium monitoring when starting or changing dosage, not an individualized ranking against clonazepam (p. 2068).
**C. Quetiapine.** Wrong, it is not risk-free: Beers advises avoiding antipsychotics except for defined indications and notes mortality concerns beyond dementia. Preserved cognition alone does not establish appropriateness, but this is not the official choice (p. 2059).
**D. Clonazepam.** Correct, the official choice is supported by the benzodiazepine warning for cognitive impairment, delirium, falls and fractures. Interpret this within review of indication and possible dependence, not as a universal ranking of the four drugs (p. 2060).

Inference for this question: the benzodiazepine warning makes clonazepam a target for considering dose reduction. The source does not establish it as the greatest risk in this particular patient without the indications for all medications (pp. 2059–2060, 2068).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria Update Expert Panel. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71:2052–2081, pp. 2059–2060, 2068 (PDF pp. 8, 9, 17). doi:10.1111/jgs.18372.
ref: Beers Criteria; Hazzard 8e · ch. 11 p. 169; ch. 22 p. 319
referenceNote: Printed IMA citation retained; checked explanation source: Hazzard 8e · p. 169, 319.

q: כיצד מוגדר "אדם קרוב" לפי "חוק החולה הנוטה למות"?
o: כל אדם שמכיר את החולה
רופא המטפל בחולה
אדם בעל קרבה משפחתית או רגשית לחולה ומסור לו
כל אדם שמבקר את החולה בבית החולים
explanation:
לפי **חוק החולה הנוטה למות (2005)**, "אדם קרוב" מוגדר כמי שקשור לחולה בקשר של **קרבה משפחתית** **או** קרבה רגשית, ושהוא מסור לחולה. ההגדרה מודעת לכך שלא כל קרוב משפחה ביולוגי בהכרח מסור לחולה, ולא כל מי שמסור הוא דווקא קרוב דם.

**א. כל אדם שמכיר את החולה.** שגויה, היכרות כשלעצמה אינה ממלאת את דרישות הקרבה, המסירות והקשר הרצוף שבסעיף 3 (עמ׳ 1 בקובץ).
**ב. רופא המטפל בחולה.** שגויה, תפקידו כרופא מטפל אינו מקנה לבדו מעמד של אדם קרוב; השאלה היא אם מתקיימים תנאי ההגדרה האישיים, ולא עצם העיסוק ברפואה (סעיף 3, עמ׳ 1 בקובץ).
**ג. אדם בעל קרבה משפחתית או רגשית לחולה ומסור לו.** נכונה, זו האפשרות המתאימה להגדרה, בצירוף הדרישה להיכרות טובה המבוססת על קשר רצוף ומתמשך לפי דעת הרופא האחראי (סעיף 3, עמ׳ 1 בקובץ).
**ד. כל אדם שמבקר את החולה בבית החולים.** שגויה, ביקור בבית החולים אינו מוכיח מסירות והיכרות טובה המבוססת על קשר מתמשך, ולכן אינו מספיק להגדרה (סעיף 3, עמ׳ 1 בקובץ).

נדרשת גם היכרות טובה המבוססת על קשר רצוף ומתמשך, לפי דעת הרופא האחראי (חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיף 3, PDF p.1).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיף 3, עמ׳ 1 בקובץ.
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: Cognitive decline is common during long-standing Parkinson disease. Which finding best supports Parkinson disease dementia rather than PD-MCI or a different timing of Lewy body dementia?
o: Objective cognitive impairment is present, but cognitive difficulties leave functional independence substantially preserved.
Dementia begins before the motor syndrome, followed later by the emergence of parkinsonian motor signs.
Multidomain cognitive decline impairs daily activities after years of well-established Parkinson motor symptoms.
Motor limitations impair daily activities, while cognitive testing and everyday cognitive abilities remain preserved.
explanation:
**Dementia in Parkinson disease requires cognitive impairment that affects everyday independence**, rather than an abnormal cognitive score alone. The source distinguishes PDD from PD-MCI by functional impact and distinguishes PDD from DLB by the timing of cognitive symptoms relative to the established motor syndrome (p. 870).
"cognitive impairment severe enough to impair activities of daily living" (p. 870).
"impairments in more than one cognitive domain on detailed neurocognitive testing." (p. 870).

**A. Objective cognitive impairment is present, but cognitive difficulties leave functional independence substantially preserved.** Wrong, preserved functional independence despite cognitive impairment fits the source’s description of PD-MCI rather than establishing dementia (p. 870).
**B. Dementia begins before the motor syndrome, followed later by the emergence of parkinsonian motor signs.** Wrong, dementia preceding the motor syndrome follows the temporal pattern classified as DLB, rather than PDD after established Parkinson disease (p. 870).
**C. Multidomain cognitive decline impairs daily activities after years of well-established Parkinson motor symptoms.** Correct, this combines the established motor disease with multidomain cognitive impairment severe enough to impair daily activities, as required by the described PDD criteria (p. 870).
**D. Motor limitations impair daily activities, while cognitive testing and everyday cognitive abilities remain preserved.** Wrong, motor disability alone does not establish dementia; the criteria require cognitive impairment and its effect on everyday activities (p. 870).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 870.
chapterTitle: Cognitive Changes in Normal and Pathologic Aging

q: What minimum lymph-node count defines adequate evaluation in the cited CRC surgical analysis?
o: A lower node-count standard solely because of age
No minimum node count for older adults
Examination of no lymph nodes after hemicolectomy
Examination of at least 12 lymph nodes
explanation:
The cited SEER analysis defines adequate lymph-node evaluation as examination of at least 12 lymph nodes (p1440).

B. No minimum node count for older adults: The analysis uses at least 12 nodes and links inadequate evaluation with inferior survival (p1440).
C. Examination of no lymph nodes after hemicolectomy: At least 12 nodes are required for adequate evaluation in the cited analysis (p1440).
A. A lower node-count standard solely because of age: Older adults were less likely to receive adequate evaluation, not assigned a lower adequacy standard (p1440).

q: Which oxaliplatin toxicity can undermine function and increase falls?
o: Peripheral neuropathy
Biliary obstruction
Liver enzyme elevations
Hemolytic uremic syndrome
explanation:
**Oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy** can turn treatment toxicity into a functional problem. Hazzard says this neuropathy “may increase the risk of falls and limit functional status”; the consequence matters because falls and impaired function are themselves associated with poorer prognosis in older adults with colon cancer (p. 1441).

**A. Peripheral neuropathy.** Correct, it is the treatment-related neurologic toxicity directly linked to falls and functional limitation in this population (p. 1441).
**B. Biliary obstruction.** Wrong, it does not identify the oxaliplatin neurotoxicity linked to falls; the chapter discusses biliary obstruction as a different clinical problem requiring palliation (pp. 1441, 1446).
**C. Liver enzyme elevations.** Wrong, it substitutes a hepatic laboratory toxicity for the peripheral-nerve toxicity that explains the functional outcome in the stem (pp. 1441, 1445).
**D. Hemolytic uremic syndrome.** Wrong, it substitutes a different drug-associated syndrome for the oxaliplatin neuropathy explicitly linked to falls and functional impairment (pp. 1441, 1445).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1441, 1445, 1446.
